[/page/1/Text/7] We sought to test a novel depression prevention approach where CBT skills are applied to goals that are important to adolescents and their families.

dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/4] Depression prevention programs for adolescents have primarily been based on cognitive-behavioral principles. Three recent meta-analyses showed that youth depression prevention programs are efficacious, although effect sizes were small, ranging from d = .16 (Horowitz & Garber, 2006) to d = .20 (Merry et al., 2012) to d = .30 (Stice, Shaw, Bohon, Marti & Rohde, 2009). The authors also examined effect sizes by type of program: indicated, which include participants with subclinical symptoms, selective, which include participants with higherthan-average risk for development of the disorder, and universal, which are administered to all members of a target population.
